```{r,echo=FALSE}
options(scipen=999)
pfix = function(c,d){
    cc = c[c!=0]
    dd = d[c!=0]
    p = paste0("{",cc,"}x^{",dd,"}",collapse="+")
    p = gsub("x^{0}","",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("x^{1}","x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("+{-","-{",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("+{1}x","+x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("-{1}x","-x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("{-1}x","-x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("{1}x","x",p,fixed=T)
    return(p)
}

dega = 2
degb = 2

while(T){
    da = dega:0
    db = degb:0
    ca = sample(-9:9,dega+1,T)
    cb = sample(-9:9,degb+1,T)
    pa = pfix(ca,da)
    pb = pfix(cb,db)
    fulllist = list()
    k = 0
    crf = numeric()
    drf = numeric()
    for(i in 1:length(da)){
        for(j in 1:length(db)){
            k = k+1
            fulllist[[k]] = c(ca[i]*cb[j],da[i]+db[j])
            crf = c(crf,ca[i]*cb[j])
            drf = c(drf,da[i]+db[j])
        }
    }
    
    dr = rev(sort(unique(drf)))
    cr = rep(0,length(dr))
    for(i in 1:length(crf)){
        c = crf[i]
        d = drf[i]
        cr[dr==d] = cr[dr==d]+c
    }
    
    prf = pfix(crf,drf)
    pr = pfix(cr,dr)
    if(min(abs(cr)) > 1 && max(abs(cr))<100 && ca[1]!=0 && cb[1]!=0){break}
}

xtra = sample(2:99,4)
ch = sort(unique(c(0,1,-1,crf,cr,-crf,-cr,-xtra,xtra)))
al1 = paste0("* ",ch,collapse="\n")

chmid = character()
for(i in ch){
    chmid = c(chmid,i)
    # if(i<0){
    #     chmid = c(chmid,i)
    # } else {
    #     chmid = c(chmid,paste0("+",i))
    # }
}
almid = paste0("* ",chmid,collapse="\n")

sol1 = paste0(1*(ch==cr[1]),collapse="")
sol2 = paste0(1*(ch==cr[2]),collapse="")
sol3 = paste0(1*(ch==cr[3]),collapse="")
sol4 = paste0(1*(ch==cr[4]),collapse="")
sol5 = paste0(1*(ch==cr[5]),collapse="")


```


Question
========

Find the coefficients ($A$ through $E$) that make the below equation true [for all](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_quantification) values of $x$.

$$\left(`r pa`\right) \cdot \left(`r pb`\right) ~=~ Ax^4+Bx^3+Cx^2+Dx+E$$

* $A=$ ##ANSWER1##
* $B=$ ##ANSWER2##
* $C=$ ##ANSWER3##
* $D=$ ##ANSWER4##
* $E=$ ##ANSWER5##


Answerlist
--------

`r al1`
`r almid`
`r almid`
`r almid`
`r almid`


Solution
========

Start with the left side.

$$\left(`r pa`\right) \cdot \left(`r pb`\right)$$

Use a box to help organize the repeated distribution of multiplication over addition. (Use a box to expand the product.)

```{css,echo=F}
.boxy td {
    border: 1px solid black;
    color: black;
    background-color: white;
  }

    background-color: rgb(200, 200, 200);
    color: black;
    border: 1px solid black;
  }
.boxy td:first-child {
    background-color: rgb(200, 200, 200);
    color: black;
    border: 1px solid black;
  }
.boxy select {
    width: 5em;
}
```

<div class="boxy">

| \* | $`r ca[1]`x^2$ | $`r ca[2]`x$ |$`r ca[3]`$|
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $`r cb[1]`x^2$ |  $`r crf[1]`x^4$  |  $`r crf[4]`x^3$  |  $`r crf[7]`x^2$  |
| $`r cb[2]`x$ | $`r crf[2]`x^3$   |  $`r crf[5]`x^2$  |  $`r crf[8]`x$  |
| $`r cb[3]`$ | $`r crf[3]`x^2$   |  $`r crf[6]`x$  |  $`r crf[9]`$  |

</div>


$$`r prf`$$

Combine like terms.

$$`r pr`$$

So, 

* $A=`r cr[1]`$
* $B=`r cr[2]`$
* $C=`r cr[3]`$
* $D=`r cr[4]`$
* $E=`r cr[5]`$
